### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis 8  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.782)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:2079)

**Proposed mechanism:** CLN8 (HGNC:2079) —DISRUPTS→ Endoplasmic Reticulum membrane protein trafficking (REACT:R-HSA-197420); Endoplasmic Reticulum membrane protein trafficking (REACT:R-HSA-197420) —DECREASES→ Lysosomal function (GO:0005741); Lysosomal function (GO:0005741) —DECREASES→ Accumulation of lipopigment (HP:0001271); Accumulation of lipopigment (HP:0001271) —LEADS_TO→ Neurodegeneration (HP:0002184); Neurodegeneration (HP:0002184) —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001250); Accumulation of lipopigment (HP:0001271) —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001250). Loss-of-function mutations in CLN8 disrupt normal ER membrane protein trafficking, which in turn impairs lysosomal function. This leads to the accumulation of lipopigments, ultimately causing neurodegeneration and seizures, characteristic phenotypes of both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a pathogenic variant in CLN8 with a demonstrably gain-of-function effect in relevant cellular models for either disease, or a lack of any significant allele frequency of deleterious variants in gnomAD. _(variant: HGNC:2079)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism involving CLN8 dysfunction and lysosomal impairment could lead to the development of targeted therapies for both MONDO:0012391 and neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis 8, potentially by enhancing lysosomal function or clearing lipopigment accumulation.
